hypothesis: On the six-message, four-context, four-future-state world with the hand-built update operator Psi of paper section 4, Theorem CS-1 predicts ~_Psi is a proper equivalence relation on M; Theorem CS-2 predicts the quotient M/~_Psi is exactly {{m0,m1},{m2,m3},{m4},{m5}} and is a common sufficient statistic (Theorem-4 sense) for the family {Psi(., c) : c in C} on M; the distractor co-occurrence quotient M/~_kappa is {{m0,m2,m4},{m1,m3,m5}} and is distinct from M/~_Psi.

controls.description: Every Psi(m, c) row is a probability distribution over the four future states (nonnegative entries summing to 1 within 1e-12); verified in tests.

At context c0, the four class-conditional distributions D_A, D_B, D_C, D_D are pairwise distinct probability vectors (0.5, 0.5, 0, 0), (0, 0, 0.5, 0.5), (1, 0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 0, 1); ensures the four Psi-classes are pairwise distinct.

The co-occurrence signature kappa is a fixed 6 x 4 integer table with row equality collapsing even-indexed and odd-indexed messages into two groups; no randomness, no clustering algorithm, no thresholds.
Equivalence classes are built by scanning every message against every other message under the relation callable; equivalent to the transitive closure of the pointwise-equality relation.

gates.criterion: The relation ~_Psi on M is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive under exhaustive enumeration.
M/~_Psi equals {{m0,m1},{m2,m3},{m4},{m5}} exactly (as a set of frozensets of messages).
For every c in C and every pair of messages in the same Psi-class, Psi(m, c) matches componentwise within 1e-12.
The co-occurrence partition M/~_kappa differs from the Psi-quotient M/~_Psi as a set of cells.
